candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the $close leaf: it is dividend-adjusted while $low/$high are raw, so subtracting/ratioing them imports future-dividend lookahead (the exact bug memory flags for this family). Swapping to $open keeps the range-position measure on one consistent raw scale without touching the otherwise strong, perfectly stable (100% positive years) structure.

This is the factor memory names by id as mixing adjusted $close with raw $high, a dividend lookahead bug no gate checks for. Replacing $close with $open removes the scale mismatch while leaving the low-turnover range/std structure that drives its 9.2 fitness intact.

The reported 0.780 nearest-archive correlation is driven by the TS_MEAN($return,10) term it shares verbatim with sibling 0168481b; the EPS/TS_MIN($low,21) valuation leg is bug-free and the stronger half of the pair. Swapping the shared term from mean-return to return-volatility keeps the valuation leg but replaces the redundant piece with a genuinely different (2nd-moment) signal.

EPS/$close divides a raw fundamental by a dividend-adjusted price, precisely the scale bug memory names for this already-seeded archive term, and recommends anchoring valuation ratios on $open instead. Fixing only that leaf leaves the return-rank spread half untouched.

Matches memory's named TS_MAX($high,21)-$close scale-mismatch family, already remutated 3x by changing the surrounding */÷ operator or grouping without success. This instead changes the field itself, $close to $open, which is the fix that was never tried.

This is the only factor in the batch normalizing $dollar_volume with CS_ZSCORE instead of rank, and dollar volume is heavily right-skewed, so a z-score is fragile to a handful of mega-cap outliers while every other dollar-volume usage here is rank-based. CS_RANK gives the same directional spread without that tail sensitivity.

Stability 0.86 with negative IC in 2009 and 2012 is exactly the positive-most-years-negative-in-two regime problem. The 63-day trailing-mean reference goes stale through the crash/rebound turn, so the up-day count is measured against a lagging benchmark exactly when the regime shifts; shortening it to 21 days lets the reference track the regime instead of lagging it.

Nearest-archive rho 0.622 against raw TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) alone shows dollar volume is dominating this product, the exact failure memory describes for un-ranked volume terms multiplied into a ratio. Ranking it first lets the EPS signal actually contribute and should also temper the 2009-2010 crisis-era instability (stability 0.86), which lines up with volume spikes swamping the factor in that period.

Half-life is 3.8 days, far shorter than every other candidate here, consistent with dividend-adjustment noise from ratioing adjusted $close against raw $high (the same scale bug flagged on several siblings in this batch) rather than a genuine fast-decaying signal. Switching to $open removes that artifact-prone mismatch while leaving the dollar-volume timing term untouched.

Turnover 0.314 and its 0.011 fitness charge are both the highest in the batch, and despite a reasonable t-stat this factor has the lowest fitness of the ten, i.e. it is paying costs it does not earn back. The likely driver is ranking noisy raw daily $dollar_volume over time; smoothing it with TS_MEAN(...,21) first, as the other dollar-volume/TS_RANK factor in this batch already does, should cut the churn.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

  1. Multiplying a bounded price ratio by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, ...) caused 2 of 4 correlation rejections because dollar_volume dominates the product — rank or demean dollar_volume before combining rather than multiplying it in raw.
  2. 4 of 19 rejections were archived trees re-proposed with only a changed window constant or an added DELAY/extra-smoothing wrapper — when mutating an archived parent, change the operator or input field, not just the constants.
  3. The fast/price_volume/low niche looks saturated: $close normalized by rolling std/min/max in the 15-63 day band produced this round's weakest accept (0.004, itself near-duplicate of a rejected subtree) plus 2 of 4 correlation rejections — shift search toward the mixed/medium and mixed/slow niches that produced this round's 4 best scores.
  4. CS_DEMEAN'd asset_turnover crossed with a short close-delta, and CS_RANK of a $return win-count, both cleared the bar only modestly (1.85, 0.89) — iterate on these with alternate fundamentals or count windows rather than repeating plain price/volume normalizations.
  5. $close/$adj_close is dividend-adjusted; $open/$high/$low/$dollar_volume are raw. This round's top factor (fitness 9.206, $high - $close over std(high-low,10)) and a 3x-remutated archive family (TS_MAX($high,21) - $close) both mix the two scales, a future-dividend lookahead bug no gate checks for. Do not subtract or ratio $close/$adj_close against $open/$high/$low.
  6. $earnings_per_share and $book_per_share are raw-scale like OHLC, so dividing either by $close/$adj_close carries the same lookahead bug. This round's rejected EPS/TS_MEAN($close,21) term inherited it from an archive parent (EPS/$close) already seeded in the archive. Anchor valuation ratios on $open instead.
  7. Normalizing a price-range numerator by $dollar_volume (mean or rank) failed the cheap screen 4 times this round (|t| 0.11-0.75). Normalize range terms by TS_STD of a same-scale price series instead.
  8. 3 rejections (6, 4, 4 shared nodes) were the same archived high-close-vs-dollar_volume subtree with only the */÷ operator or grouping changed. An operator swap around an archived subtree doesn't evade archive_subtree; change the window or field instead.
  9. Swapping the aggregator on one term (TS_MIN vs TS_MEAN on $low,21) barely moved correlation (rho 0.997). A same-window aggregator swap on a single term won't clear the correlation gate.
  10. Smoothing a slow fundamental with a long TS_MEAN (roa, 126d) stayed near-identical to the raw field (rho 0.837) since fundamentals update quarterly. Pair fundamentals with a fast-moving second term rather than just smoothing them.
  11. Wrapping one operand of a ratio in CS_RANK ($dollar_volume ranked inside TS_MEAN) didn't decorrelate from the unranked version (rho 0.911). Adding a rank around a sub-term is a weak move against the correlation gate.
  12. EMA-crossover forms correlate highly across window choices and ratio-vs-difference framing (rho 0.825 between two differently-windowed variants this round). Treat EMA-crossover as one already-covered family, not new proposals per window pair.
